title: Premature, imprudent and illegal
primary_topics: Installment-proclamation critique column May 19, 2013 -- second of automated-elections quadrilogy (E100 May 11 → A458 May 19 → B19 May 26 → E99 June 2 → A456 June 16)

Comelec installment-proclamation of 9 senators: May 16 first batch -- Grace Poe + Loren Legarda + Alan Peter Cayetano + Chiz Escudero + Nancy Binay + Sonny Angara (six); May 17 second batch -- Bam Aquino + Koko Pimentel + Sonny Trillanes (three); pending final canvass for last three -- Cynthia Villar + JV Ejercito + possibly Gringo Honasan

Three-prong indictment: 'premature, imprudent and illegal' -- 'no legal and factual basis... with due respect to the Comelec'; 'Why the indecent haste? Why rush to proclaim without legal or factual basis? Why not wait for two days, just two days, and then proclaim all 12 legally and unquestionably?'

Rule-and-exception doctrine: entrenched-legal-and-commonsensical rule = 'winners can be proclaimed only after all ballots have been officially canvassed'; exception = 'when leading candidates posts an insurmountable lead, i.e., remaining uncanvassed ballots will not adversely affect results'; Comelec 'meticulously and correctly invoked this rule and exception when it instructed provincial and city boards of canvassers to proclaim local winners -- it should apply the same standard to its own proclamations'

50M-ballots illustrative example: if 90% (45M) canvassed and first 9 candidates each above 20M while others below 15M → even if remaining 5M uncanvassed votes went entirely to others, none could overtake the nine → exception applies

Real-facts diagnosis: May 16 proclamations covered only 72 of 304 COCs (~13M of 52M registered voters); 'definitely, then, the unreported votes are several times more than the canvassed votes'; even with 70% turnout, uncanvassed ballots 'will easily swamp canvassed ones' → 'exception cannot apply'

'Group canvass reports' novelty: Comelec belatedly justified earlier proclamations by 'so-called group canvass reports'; CJP: 'In my long years as a lawyer, this is my first time to hear of these electoral instruments'; 'law and settled jurisprudence require official COCs, not any other documents, as bases of senatorial proclamations'; if Comelec wants to change rules, 'required by law to first publish its new rules and wait for the mandatory lapse of seven days after publication before it can use the new rules'

SET-jurisdictional concern: legal-enigma -- 'if the final canvass did not confirm their victory, not even the Comelec or the Supreme Court could unseat them' because once proclamation is made, 'the sole judge... of all contests relating to the election, returns and qualifications of senators is the Senate Electoral Tribunal' (6 senators + 3 SC justices); SET 'can act only after the Senate is convened in late July'; by then 'the nine would be sitting in the Senate'; not all who 'obtained enough votes can sit because Senate has only 24 members'; 'undeserved legal enigma'

'2016 destabilization risk' warning: 'baseless and premature proclamations should never be repeated, especially during the presidential election in 2016. Otherwise, they could destabilize and bring unintended consequences on our democracy'

Shining-moment close: if 9 proclamations confirmed by final canvass, 'they should be given new certificates of proclamation, containing the legal justification for their victory -- namely, the correct number of votes and rank they garnered to avoid giving them the dubious distinction of being the only senators in our country's history with premature, imprudent and illegal proclamations'; commends Nancy Binay + Koko Pimentel for refusing-to-participate (Pimentel: 'candidates should not only win the elections fairly but also strictly observe the law'); 'Kudos to Romulo Macalintal' for asking proclaimed senators to 'return or surrender their certificates of proclamation... as a shining moment of the democratic process'; CJP-tribute: 'Macalintal's exemplary advocacy is his own shining moment for the rule of law and democracy'
sub_topics: With due respect to Commission on Elections, CJP finds no legal and factual basis for proclamation in installment of six senatorial candidates
Grace Poe, Loren Legarda, Alan Peter Cayetano, Chiz Escudero, Nancy Binay and Sonny Angara on May 16
And another three (Bam Aquino, Koko Pimentel and Sonny Trillanes) on next day, May 17
Comelec was reported to be trying to finish official canvass at late hour on third day, yesterday May 18
(past CJP's deadline for this column), or today
And to proclaim last three winners (Cynthia Villar, JV Ejercito and possibly Gringo Honasan)
Final canvass may moot prematurity of two earlier proclamations
But it will not lessen their baselessness and illegality at their inception
Merely raises new questions: No one was chasing Comelec, why indecent haste?
Why rush to proclaim without legal or factual basis?
Why not wait for two days, just two days, and then proclaim all 12 legally and unquestionably?
Let us dig deeper
Entrenched legal and commonsensical rule is that winners can be proclaimed only after all ballots have been officially canvassed
Exception to this rule is when leading candidate(s) posts insurmountable lead
That is, when remaining uncanvassed ballots will not adversely affect results
Comelec meticulously and correctly invoked this rule and exception when it instructed provincial and city boards of canvassers to proclaim local winners
It should apply same standard to its own proclamations
To understand exception, imagine total of 50 million ballots were cast
Of which 90 percent or 45 million were canvassed
Imagine further that each of first nine senatorial candidates obtained more than 20 million votes
While each of other candidates had less than 15 million
Here, even if remaining 10 percent (5 million) uncanvassed votes were added to each of other candidates
None of them could overtake nine
In these imagined facts, exception applies and first nine may be proclaimed
Look now at real facts
When six candidates were proclaimed on May 16, official canvass of Comelec covered only 72 out of 304 certificates of canvass (COCs)
These 72 COCs represented just little more than 13 million of country's 52 million registered voters
Definitely, then, unreported votes are several times more than canvassed votes
Even if only 70 percent of registered voters actually voted, still uncanvassed ballots will easily swamp canvassed ones
Hence, exception cannot apply
Belatedly, Comelec alleges that its two earlier proclamations are justified by so-called 'group canvass reports'
In CJP's long years as lawyer, this is first time to hear of these electoral instruments
In any event, law and settled jurisprudence require official COCs, not any other documents, as bases of senatorial proclamations
If Comelec wants to change its rules of proclamation even at risk of offending jurisprudence
It is required by law to first publish its new rules and wait for mandatory lapse of seven days after publication before it can use new rules
Clearly, then, first two proclamations were premature and illegal
Worse, if final canvass did not confirm their victory, not even Comelec or Supreme Court could unseat them
Because once proclamation is made, 'sole judge', says Constitution, 'of all contests relating to election, returns and qualifications' of senators is Senate Electoral Tribunal (SET)
Composed of six senators and three Supreme Court justices
SET can act only after Senate is convened in late July
By that time, nine would be sitting in Senate
On other hand, not all those who obtained enough votes can sit because Senate has only 24 members
Then, country would be faced with undeserved legal enigma
At this point, CJP hopes readers realize prematurity and illegality of two earlier proclamations
Unless upheld and cured by final canvass, could bring unwarranted and unnecessary legal consequences
Baseless and premature proclamations should never be repeated, especially during presidential election in 2016
Otherwise, they could destabilize and bring unintended consequences on our democracy
If and when proclamation of nine is confirmed by final canvass
CJP believes they should be given new certificates of proclamation
Containing legal justification for their victory -- namely, correct number of votes and rank they garnered
To avoid giving them dubious distinction of being only senators in our country's history with premature, imprudent and illegal proclamations
CJP cannot close this piece without applauding courage and wisdom of Nancy Binay and Koko Pimentel
In refusing to participate in tainted proclamation rites
Pimentel labeled proclamation rites as improper, arguing that candidates should not only win elections fairly but also strictly observe law
Kudos also to Romulo Macalintal for calling public attention to this legal impasse
And for asking proclaimed senators to 'return or surrender their certificates of proclamation... as a shining moment... of the democratic process'
CJP dares say that Macalintal's exemplary advocacy is his own shining moment for rule of law and democracy

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes the second installment of his automated-elections quadrilogy -- six days after E100 (Let's all vote Monday) and one week before B19 (Most important investment incentive) -- delivering a sharp three-adjective indictment of the Comelec's installment proclamation of 9 senators on May 16-17 while only 72 of 304 COCs had been canvassed. With due respect to the Comelec, CJ finds no legal and factual basis for the proclamation in installment of six senatorial candidates (Grace Poe, Loren Legarda, Alan Peter Cayetano, Chiz Escudero, Nancy Binay and Sonny Angara) on May 16, and another three (Bam Aquino, Koko Pimentel and Sonny Trillanes) on the next day, May 17. Rule and exception: the Comelec was reported to be trying to finish the official canvass at a late hour on the third day, yesterday May 18 (past CJ's deadline for this column), or today, and to proclaim the last three winners (Cynthia Villar, JV Ejercito and possibly Gringo Honasan) -- this final canvass may moot the prematurity of the two earlier proclamations, but it will not lessen their baselessness and illegality at their inception; it merely raises new questions: no one was chasing the Comelec, why the indecent haste? Why rush to proclaim without legal or factual basis? Why not wait for two days, just two days, and then proclaim all 12 legally and unquestionably? Let us dig deeper. The entrenched legal and commonsensical rule is that winners can be proclaimed only after all ballots have been officially canvassed; the exception to this rule is when the leading candidate(s) posts an insurmountable lead, that is, when the remaining uncanvassed ballots will not adversely affect the results -- the Comelec meticulously and correctly invoked this rule and exception when it instructed the provincial and city boards of canvassers to proclaim the local winners; it should apply the same standard to its own proclamations. To understand the exception, imagine that a total of 50 million ballots were cast in an election, of which 90% (45 million) were canvassed; imagine further that each of the first nine senatorial candidates obtained more than 20 million votes while each of the other candidates had less than 15 million -- here, even if the remaining 10% (5 million) uncanvassed votes were added to each of the other candidates, none of them could overtake the nine; in these imagined facts, the exception applies and the first nine may be proclaimed. Look now at the real facts: when the six candidates were proclaimed on May 16, the official canvass of the Comelec covered only 72 out of the 304 COCs -- these 72 COCs represented just a little more than 13 million of the country's 52 million registered voters; definitely, then, the unreported votes are several times more than the canvassed votes; even if only 70% of the registered voters actually voted, still the uncanvassed ballots will easily swamp the canvassed ones -- hence, the exception cannot apply. Belatedly, the Comelec alleges that its two earlier proclamations are justified by so-called 'group canvass reports' -- in CJ's long years as a lawyer, this is his first time to hear of these electoral instruments; in any event, law and settled jurisprudence require official COCs, not any other documents, as bases of senatorial proclamations; if the Comelec wants to change its rules of proclamation even at the risk of offending jurisprudence, it is required by law to first publish its new rules and wait for the mandatory lapse of seven days after publication before it can use the new rules. Legal enigma: clearly, then, the first two proclamations were premature and illegal -- worse, if the final canvass did not confirm their victory, not even the Comelec or the SC could unseat them; because once proclamation is made, 'the sole judge,' says the Constitution, 'of all contests relating to the election, returns and qualifications' of senators is the SET (composed of 6 senators and 3 SC justices); the SET can act only after the Senate is convened in late July -- by that time, the nine would be sitting in the Senate; on the other hand, not all those who obtained enough votes can sit because the Senate has only 24 members; then, the country would be faced with an undeserved legal enigma. At this point, CJ hopes readers realize that the prematurity and illegality of the two earlier proclamations, unless upheld and cured by the final canvass, could bring unwarranted and unnecessary legal consequences; baseless and premature proclamations should never be repeated, especially during the presidential election in 2016 -- otherwise, they could destabilize and bring unintended consequences on our democracy. Shining moment: if and when the proclamation of the nine is confirmed by the final canvass, CJ believes they should be given new certificates of proclamation, containing the legal justification for their victory -- namely, the correct number of votes and rank they garnered to avoid giving them the dubious distinction of being the only senators in our country's history with premature, imprudent and illegal proclamations. CJ cannot close this piece without applauding the courage and wisdom of Nancy Binay and Koko Pimentel in refusing to participate in the tainted proclamation rites -- Pimentel labeled the proclamation rites as improper, arguing that candidates should not only win the elections fairly but also strictly observe the law; kudos also to Romulo Macalintal for calling public attention to this legal impasse and for asking the proclaimed senators to 'return or surrender their certificates of proclamation... as a shining moment of the democratic process'; CJ dares say that Macalintal's exemplary advocacy is his own shining moment for the rule of law and democracy.
